questions.q: What do you provide to Data Loader's Export operation to control which records and fields come out?
options: A list of record names typed into a text box
A Flow that runs on a schedule
A SOQL query, built with the field picker or edited directly
Nothing; it always exports every field of every record
questions.explain: The export wizard builds a SOQL query, and you can edit that query text directly.

questions.q: What is the output of a Data Loader export?
options: A CSV file
A new custom object in the org
A SOQL view in Setup
An Apex class
questions.explain: Exports are written to a CSV file you choose.

questions.q: What is the difference between Export and Export All?
options: Export All exports every object at once
Export All runs faster by skipping the query
There is no difference; the names are interchangeable
Export All also includes Recycle Bin (deleted) and archived records
questions.explain: Export returns current records; Export All also returns soft-deleted and archived ones.

questions.q: Which SOQL clauses from Chapter One can you use in a Data Loader export query?
options: Only SELECT
SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT
None; exports use a separate query language
Only WHERE
questions.explain: The export query is real SOQL, so the familiar clauses apply.

questions.q: Why is exporting a good first step before you change or delete records?
options: Salesforce requires an export before any update will run
Exporting locks the records so nobody else can edit them
It gives you a CSV copy of the original values to fall back on
It automatically creates an undo button in the org
questions.explain: An export taken before a change is a simple, real safety net if the load goes wrong.
